text: 悄悄是别离的笙箫，夏虫也为我沉默，沉默是今晚的康桥
pinyin: qiāo qiāo shì bié lí de shēng xiāo, xià chóng yě wèi wǒ chén mò, chén mò shì jīn wǎn de kāng qiáo
literal: quietly · is · parting · 's · reed pipes, summer insects · also · for · me · fall silent, silence · is · tonight · 's · Cambridge
natural: softly, the music of farewell is the quiet; even the summer insects fall silent for me; tonight Cambridge is silence itself

meaning.en: Xu Zhimo's closing stanza of 'Saying Goodbye to Cambridge Again': at parting the only music is hushed stillness, and the whole scene falls silent with the poet.
meaning.zh: 徐志摩《再别康桥》的结尾：离别时唯一的乐声是悄然无声，连夏虫也为诗人沉默，整个康桥都沉默了。

equivalents: a silence that says goodbye
the quiet music of parting

examples.zh: 毕业晚会上，主持人念起“悄悄是别离的笙箫，夏虫也为我沉默，沉默是今晚的康桥”，全场安静了下来。
examples.en: At the graduation party the host read 'quietly is the reed pipe of parting; even the summer insects fall silent for me', and the whole hall went quiet.

examples.zh: 离开校园前的最后一夜，他想起了“悄悄是别离的笙箫，夏虫也为我沉默，沉默是今晚的康桥”。
examples.en: On his last night on campus he thought of the lines 'quietly is the reed pipe of parting; even the summer insects fall silent for me'.

story.en: Xu Zhimo wrote 'Saying Goodbye to Cambridge Again' in November 1928 on his voyage home from England, recalling his time at King's College, Cambridge, in 1920-22.
story.zh: 1928年11月，徐志摩从英国乘船回国途中写下《再别康桥》，追忆1920至1922年在剑桥大学的时光。

usage.en: Quoted at farewells, especially graduations. The lines close the poem, which begins 轻轻的我走了; in the original the first two clauses are separated by a semicolon. The poem was written in November 1928.
usage.zh: 多在毕业、送别场合引用，是全诗的结尾，全诗以“轻轻的我走了”开篇。原诗前两句之间为分号。此诗作于1928年11月。

text: 你有你的，我有我的，方向
pinyin: nǐ yǒu nǐ de, wǒ yǒu wǒ de, fāng xiàng
literal: you · have · your, I · have · my, direction
natural: you have your own direction, I have mine

meaning.en: A line from Xu Zhimo's 'By Chance': two people meet briefly, then each goes on in a separate direction.
meaning.zh: 徐志摩《偶然》中的诗句：两人偶然相遇，随即各自走向不同的方向。

equivalents: each goes their own way
ships that pass in the night

examples.zh: 毕业后同学们天各一方，真是“你有你的，我有我的，方向”。
examples.en: After graduation the classmates scattered, truly 'you have your direction, I have mine'.

examples.zh: 恋情结束时，她只说了一句“你有你的，我有我的，方向”。
examples.en: When the relationship ended she said only, 'you have your direction, I have mine'.

story.en: Xu Zhimo's short poem 'By Chance' (1926) begins 我是天空里的一片云 and was later set to music; this is its second stanza.
story.zh: 徐志摩《偶然》（1926年）以“我是天空里的一片云”开篇，后来被谱成歌曲；这一句出自第二节。

usage.en: Often quoted when people part or drift apart, gently and without blame. The sentence continues 你记得也好，最好你忘掉 ('remember it if you like, better still forget').
usage.zh: 常用来表示分别、渐行渐远，语气温和、不带责备。下文接“你记得也好，最好你忘掉”。

text: 北国的秋，却特别地来得清，来得静，来得悲凉
pinyin: běi guó de qiū, què tè bié de lái de qīng, lái de jìng, lái de bēi liáng
literal: northern · land · 's · autumn, yet · especially · come · clear, come · still, come · desolate
natural: autumn in the north comes with a special clarity, stillness and melancholy

meaning.en: Yu Dafu's famous description of autumn in Beijing: it arrives clear, quiet and tinged with sadness.
meaning.zh: 郁达夫对北平秋天的著名描写：来得清爽、安静，又带着悲凉。

equivalents: autumn arrives clear, still and sorrowful
the melancholy of a northern autumn

examples.zh: 郁达夫写道：“北国的秋，却特别地来得清，来得静，来得悲凉。”
examples.en: Yu Dafu wrote: 'Autumn in the north comes with a special clarity, stillness and melancholy.'

examples.zh: 站在胡同口望着落叶，他想起了“北国的秋，却特别地来得清，来得静，来得悲凉”。
examples.en: Standing at the mouth of the lane watching the leaves fall, he thought of 'autumn in the north comes clear, still and melancholy'.

story.en: Yu Dafu wrote 'Autumn in the Old Capital' in August 1934 after visiting Beiping (Beijing); it became one of the best-known modern Chinese prose essays.
story.zh: 1934年8月，郁达夫游历北平后写下《故都的秋》，成为现代散文名篇。

usage.en: Quoted in essays and school compositions about autumn and old Beijing. It sets the mood of the whole essay, in which Yu Dafu contrasts the northern autumn with the southern one.
usage.zh: 常见于写秋天和老北京的文章、作文。这句定下全文基调，文中作者拿北国之秋与南国之秋作对比。

text: 洗手的时候，日子从水盆里过去；吃饭的时候，日子从饭碗里过去
pinyin: xǐ shǒu de shí hou, rì zi cóng shuǐ pén lǐ guò qù, chī fàn de shí hou, rì zi cóng fàn wǎn lǐ guò qù
literal: wash · hands · 's · time, days · from · water · basin · in · pass · by; eat · meal · 's · time, days · from · rice · bowl · in · pass · by
natural: when I wash my hands, the days slip away in the basin; when I eat, the days slip away in the bowl

meaning.en: Zhu Ziqing's image of time draining away through the smallest daily acts, a classic reminder of how fast days go.
meaning.zh: 朱自清笔下的光阴流逝：洗手、吃饭这些日常小事之间，日子悄悄过去。

equivalents: time slips through our fingers
the days drain away unnoticed

examples.zh: 朱自清写道：“洗手的时候，日子从水盆里过去；吃饭的时候，日子从饭碗里过去。”
examples.en: Zhu Ziqing wrote: 'When I wash my hands, the days slip away in the basin; when I eat, they slip away in the bowl.'

examples.zh: 临近期末，她想起“洗手的时候，日子从水盆里过去；吃饭的时候，日子从饭碗里过去”，不敢再拖了。
examples.en: With the end of term near, she remembered 'the days slip away in the basin as I wash, in the bowl as I eat', and dared not put things off any longer.

story.en: Zhu Ziqing wrote the prose piece 'Hurrying' (《匆匆》) in March 1922, when he was in his early twenties.
story.zh: 朱自清1922年3月写下散文《匆匆》，当时他二十出头。

usage.en: A staple of school essays on cherishing time; from a prose piece that is on the Chinese school syllabus.
usage.zh: 常用于珍惜时间主题的作文，所出散文《匆匆》是语文课本名篇。

text: 但是，聪明的，你告诉我，我们的日子为什么一去不复返呢
pinyin: dàn shì, cōng míng de, nǐ gào sù wǒ, wǒ men de rì zi wèi shén me yī qù bù fù fǎn ne
literal: but, clever · one, you · tell · me, our · days · why · once · go · not · return · ?
natural: but tell me, you clever one, why do our days go and never come back?

meaning.en: Zhu Ziqing's rhetorical question on why time, once gone, never returns.
meaning.zh: 朱自清的设问：时间为什么一去就不再回来。

equivalents: why do the days never return?
time once gone is gone for good

examples.zh: 朱自清问道：“但是，聪明的，你告诉我，我们的日子为什么一去不复返呢？”
examples.en: Zhu Ziqing asks: 'But tell me, you clever one, why do our days go and never come back?'

examples.zh: 作文开头他引用了“但是，聪明的，你告诉我，我们的日子为什么一去不复返呢”。
examples.en: He opened his essay by quoting 'but tell me, you clever one, why do our days go and never come back?'

story.en: From Zhu Ziqing's prose piece 'Hurrying' (1922), where he watches the days pass and asks why they cannot return.
story.zh: 出自朱自清散文《匆匆》（1922年），作者目睹日子溜走，追问它们为何不再回来。

usage.en: Quoted in writing about the passing of time. It is the question at the heart of the essay, which has no answer, only a sense of loss.
usage.zh: 多用于写时光流逝的文章。这是全文的核心设问，文中没有答案，只留下怅惘。

text: 墙角的花！当你孤芳自赏时，天地便小了
pinyin: qiáng jiǎo de huā, dāng nǐ gū fāng zì shǎng shí, tiān dì biàn xiǎo le
literal: wall · corner · 's · flower, when · you · lone · fragrance · self · admire · time, heaven · earth · then · small · (particle)
natural: flower in the corner of the wall! when you admire only yourself, your world shrinks

meaning.en: A short poem by Bing Xin warning that self-admiration narrows one's world.
meaning.zh: 冰心的小诗：只知自我欣赏，眼界就会变得狭小。

equivalents: pride shuts out the world
self-admiration narrows the world

examples.zh: 冰心说：“墙角的花！当你孤芳自赏时，天地便小了。”
examples.en: Bing Xin said: 'Flower in the corner of the wall! When you admire only yourself, your world shrinks.'

examples.zh: 老师在评语里写了“墙角的花！当你孤芳自赏时，天地便小了”，提醒他谦虚。
examples.en: In her comments the teacher wrote 'flower in the corner of the wall! when you admire only yourself, your world shrinks', to remind him to be modest.

story.en: Bing Xin's 'Stars' (《繁星》, 1923) is a collection of 164 short poems, written under the influence of Tagore's 'Stray Birds'.
story.zh: 冰心的《繁星》（1923年）是一部小诗集，共164首，受泰戈尔《飞鸟集》影响。

usage.en: Used to advise humility. It is a miniature poem from the collection 《繁星》 and plays on the set phrase 孤芳自赏.
usage.zh: 用来劝人谦虚。出自小诗集《繁星》，化用成语“孤芳自赏”。

text: 母亲啊！天上的风雨来了，鸟儿躲到它的巢里；心中的风雨来了，我只躲到你的怀里
pinyin: mǔ qīn a, tiān shàng de fēng yǔ lái le, niǎo ér duǒ dào tā de cháo lǐ, xīn zhōng de fēng yǔ lái le, wǒ zhǐ duǒ dào nǐ de huái lǐ
literal: mother · (particle), sky · above · 's · wind · rain · come · (particle), bird · hide · into · its · nest · in; heart · within · 's · wind · rain · come · (particle), I · only · hide · into · your · bosom · in
natural: mother! when storms come in the sky, birds hide in their nests; when storms come in my heart, I hide only in your arms

meaning.en: Bing Xin's tribute to a mother's love as the one refuge from life's troubles.
meaning.zh: 冰心赞美母爱的小诗：心中遇到风雨，母亲的怀抱是唯一的避风港。

equivalents: a mother's arms are the only shelter
a mother's love is a safe harbour

examples.zh: 母亲节那天，他在贺卡上抄下了“母亲啊！天上的风雨来了，鸟儿躲到它的巢里；心中的风雨来了，我只躲到你的怀里”。
examples.en: On Mother's Day he copied onto the card, 'mother! when storms come in the sky, birds hide in their nests; when storms come in my heart, I hide only in your arms'.

examples.zh: 朗诵比赛上，她读了“母亲啊！天上的风雨来了，鸟儿躲到它的巢里；心中的风雨来了，我只躲到你的怀里”，听得许多人红了眼眶。
examples.en: At the recitation contest she read 'mother! when storms come in the sky...', and many listeners' eyes grew moist.

story.en: From Bing Xin's collection of short poems 'Stars' (《繁星》, 1923); motherhood is one of her best-known themes.
story.zh: 出自冰心小诗集《繁星》（1923年）；母爱是她最著名的主题之一。

usage.en: Quoted in praise of mothers, especially around Mother's Day and in school recitals.
usage.zh: 多用来赞美母亲，常见于母亲节和学校朗诵。

text: 围在城里的人想逃出来，城外的人想冲进去
pinyin: wéi zài chéng lǐ de rén xiǎng táo chū lái, chéng wài de rén xiǎng chōng jìn qù
variants: 城外的人想冲进去，城里的人想逃出来
literal: surrounded · in · city · inside · 's · people · want · escape · out, city · outside · 's · people · want · rush · in
natural: those besieged inside the city want to get out; those outside want to get in

meaning.en: Qian Zhongshu's image, from the novel Fortress Besieged, of people who always want what lies on the other side, as with marriage or a career.
meaning.zh: 钱钟书《围城》中的比喻：城里的人想出去，城外的人想进来，婚姻、职业乃至人生的愿望大都如此。

equivalents: the grass is always greener on the other side
those in want out, those out want in

examples.zh: 围在城里的人想逃出来，城外的人想冲进去，对婚姻、对职业都是如此。
examples.en: Those inside the fortress want out and those outside want in, whether it is marriage or a career.

examples.zh: 读完《围城》，她常想起“围在城里的人想逃出来，城外的人想冲进去”这句话。
examples.en: Since finishing Fortress Besieged she often recalls the line 'those inside the fortress want out, those outside want in'.

story.en: In Qian Zhongshu's novel 'Fortress Besieged' (1947) a character quotes a saying about the 'fortress' of marriage; the novel's title becomes a metaphor for this longing.
story.zh: 钱钟书长篇小说《围城》（1947年）借人物之口说出这个比喻，书名“围城”也成为这一心态的象征。

usage.en: Usually quoted in the shortened, reordered form 城外的人想冲进去，城里的人想逃出来, which is how most people remember it; the original wording is given here as the headword. Used about marriage, jobs, and wanting what one lacks.
usage.zh: 今天更常见的是调换语序的说法“城外的人想冲进去，城里的人想逃出来”，本条以原文为主形。多用于谈婚姻、职业，以及人总想要自己没有的东西。

text: 于千万人之中遇见你所要遇见的人，于千万年之中，时间的无涯的荒野里，没有早一步，也没有晚一步，刚巧赶上了，那也没有别的话可说，唯有轻轻地问一声：噢，你也在这里吗
pinyin: yú qiān wàn rén zhī zhōng yù jiàn nǐ suǒ yào yù jiàn de rén, yú qiān wàn nián zhī zhōng, shí jiān de wú yá de huāng yě lǐ, méi yǒu zǎo yī bù, yě méi yǒu wǎn yī bù, gāng qiǎo gǎn shàng le, nà yě méi yǒu bié de huà kě shuō, wéi yǒu qīng qīng de wèn yī shēng, ō, nǐ yě zài zhè lǐ ma
literal: at · thousand · ten-thousand · people · among · meet · you · wanted · to meet · person, at · thousand · ten-thousand · years · among, time · 's · boundless · wilderness · in, not · early · one step, also · not · late · one step, just · caught · up, then · also · no · other · words · can · say, only · softly · ask · one sound: oh, you · also · are · here · (particle)
natural: among thousands upon thousands you meet the one you were meant to meet, neither a step too early nor too late, and all you can say is a soft 'Oh, you are here too?'

meaning.en: Eileen Chang's celebrated passage on fated meeting: in the vastness of time and people, two lives touch at exactly the right moment and need only a quiet greeting.
meaning.zh: 张爱玲谈缘分的名段：在茫茫人海和无涯的时间里，恰好遇见那个人，不早不晚，只需轻轻问一句。

equivalents: meeting at just the right moment
fated to meet

examples.zh: 婚礼上，司仪朗诵了“于千万人之中遇见你所要遇见的人，于千万年之中，时间的无涯的荒野里，没有早一步，也没有晚一步，刚巧赶上了，那也没有别的话可说，唯有轻轻地问一声：噢，你也在这里吗”
examples.en: At the wedding the master of ceremonies read out the passage beginning 'among thousands upon thousands you meet the one you were meant to meet'.

examples.zh: 她把“于千万人之中遇见你所要遇见的人，于千万年之中，时间的无涯的荒野里，没有早一步，也没有晚一步，刚巧赶上了，那也没有别的话可说，唯有轻轻地问一声：噢，你也在这里吗”抄进了日记。
examples.en: She copied the whole passage of Eileen Chang's, 'among thousands upon thousands you meet the one you were meant to meet...', into her diary.

story.en: 'Love' (《爱》) is a very short prose piece by Eileen Chang about a girl who meets a young man by chance at the back gate on a spring evening and never sees him again; this is its opening paragraph.
story.zh: 《爱》是张爱玲的一篇极短散文，写一个女孩在春夜后门口偶遇一位年轻人，此后再未相见；这是文章第一段。

usage.en: Usually quoted in part, often just 没有早一步，也没有晚一步 or the closing 噢，你也在这里吗; popular on wedding cards and in writing about fate. Given here in full.
usage.zh: 常被截取引用，如“没有早一步，也没有晚一步”或结尾“噢，你也在这里吗”，流行于婚礼贺卡和谈缘分的文字，这里收全文。

text: 生命是一袭华美的袍，爬满了蚤子
pinyin: shēng mìng shì yī xí huá měi de páo, pá mǎn le zǎo zi
literal: life · is · one · set · splendid · 's · robe, crawl · full · (particle) · fleas
natural: life is a gorgeous robe crawling with fleas

meaning.en: Eileen Chang's bittersweet image: life looks splendid from outside, but is riddled with small irritations.
meaning.zh: 张爱玲的名句：生命外表华美，内里却爬满了令人烦恼的小事。

equivalents: beauty with a sting in it
life is gorgeous, but riddled with annoyances

examples.zh: 她常引用张爱玲的“生命是一袭华美的袍，爬满了蚤子”来自嘲生活琐碎。
examples.en: She often quotes Eileen Chang's 'life is a gorgeous robe crawling with fleas' to mock the pettiness of daily life.

examples.zh: 读到“生命是一袭华美的袍，爬满了蚤子”，同学们都笑了，又沉默了。
examples.en: On reading 'life is a gorgeous robe crawling with fleas', the students laughed and then fell silent.

story.en: Eileen Chang's essay 'Dream of Genius' (《天才梦》) won an honourable mention in a 1939 essay competition run by the magazine 《西风》.
story.zh: 张爱玲的散文《天才梦》在1939年《西风》杂志征文中获奖。

usage.en: Quoted for wry reflections on life's blemishes. Eileen Chang wrote the essay at about the age of eighteen, and the phrase is the best-known line in it.
usage.zh: 用来苦笑着感叹生活的瑕疵。张爱玲写此文时约十八岁，这句是全文最著名的一句。

text: 出名要趁早
pinyin: chū míng yào chèn zǎo
literal: become famous · must · seize · early
natural: get famous while you are young

meaning.en: Eileen Chang's much-quoted advice that fame should come early, because it brings less joy when it comes late.
meaning.zh: 张爱玲的常引之语：成名要趁早，来得太晚，快乐也就不那么痛快。

equivalents: strike while the iron is hot
make your name while you are young

examples.zh: 张爱玲说过“出名要趁早”，所以他一毕业就开始投稿。
examples.en: Eileen Chang said 'get famous early', so he began submitting articles as soon as he graduated.

examples.zh: “出名要趁早”成了不少年轻作者的口头禅。
examples.en: 'Get famous while you are young' has become a catchphrase of many young writers.

origin.source: 张爱玲《〈传奇〉再版的话》（1944年）

story.en: In the preface to the expanded edition of her story collection 《传奇》 (1944), Eileen Chang wrote that fame must come early to be fully enjoyed.
story.zh: 张爱玲在小说集《传奇》增订本的序言《〈传奇〉再版的话》（1944年）中写下这句话。

usage.en: Often used half-jokingly by young people about ambition and success; the full original sentence is 出名要趁早呀，来得太晚的话，快乐也不那么痛快.
usage.zh: 年轻人常半开玩笑地用来谈抱负和成功；原文为“出名要趁早呀，来得太晚的话，快乐也不那么痛快”。

text: 娶了红玫瑰，久而久之，红的变了墙上的一抹蚊子血，白的还是床前明月光
pinyin: qǔ le hóng méi guī, jiǔ ér jiǔ zhī, hóng de biàn le qiáng shàng de yī mǒ wén zi xiě, bái de hái shì chuáng qián míng yuè guāng
literal: marry · (particle) · red · rose, long · and · long · of it, the red one · turns into · (particle) · wall · on · 's · one smear · mosquito · blood, the white one · still · is · 'before bed · bright · moon · light'
natural: marry the red rose and in time she becomes a smear of mosquito blood on the wall, while the white one stays 'moonlight before my bed'

meaning.en: Eileen Chang's wry take on desire: whichever woman a man chooses, the one he did not choose seems the better.
meaning.zh: 张爱玲对欲望的冷眼：男人无论选了谁，没选的那个总显得更好。

equivalents: the grass is always greener on the other side
you always want the one you did not choose

examples.zh: 有人引用“娶了红玫瑰，久而久之，红的变了墙上的一抹蚊子血，白的还是床前明月光”来感叹人心不足。
examples.en: Some quote 'marry the red rose and in time she becomes a smear of mosquito blood on the wall, while the white one stays moonlight before my bed' to sigh over human insatiability.

examples.zh: 影评人在文章开头引了“娶了红玫瑰，久而久之，红的变了墙上的一抹蚊子血，白的还是床前明月光”。
examples.en: The film critic opened the article by quoting 'marry the red rose and in time she becomes a smear of mosquito blood on the wall...'.

origin.source: 张爱玲《红玫瑰与白玫瑰》（1944年）

story.en: From Eileen Chang's novella 'Red Rose and White Rose' (1944), describing the hero Zhenbao's changing feelings for the two women in his life.
story.zh: 出自张爱玲中篇小说《红玫瑰与白玫瑰》（1944年），写男主人公振保对生命中两个女人感情的变化。

usage.en: Quoted about love and the habit of wanting what one lacks. The next clause runs 娶了白玫瑰，白的便是衣服上沾的一粒饭黏子，红的却是心口上一颗朱砂痣. 床前明月光 is the first line of Li Bai's 'Quiet Night Thought'. The passage reflects the character's view, not the author's advice.
usage.zh: 用来谈爱情和人心不足。下文接“娶了白玫瑰，白的便是衣服上沾的一粒饭黏子，红的却是心口上一颗朱砂痣”。“床前明月光”是李白《静夜思》首句。这段话是小说人物的看法，并非作者的劝告。

text: 两脚踏中西文化，一心评宇宙文章
pinyin: liǎng jiǎo tà zhōng xī wén huà, yī xīn píng yǔ zhòu wén zhāng
literal: two · feet · tread · China · West · culture, one · heart · appraise · universe · writings
natural: with one foot in Chinese and one in Western culture, my heart appraises the writings of the universe

meaning.en: Lin Yutang's self-composed couplet describing his life as a bridge between Chinese and Western culture.
meaning.zh: 林语堂自题联：两脚站在中西两种文化上，一颗心评论天地间一切文章。

equivalents: a foot in both cultures
a bridge between East and West

examples.zh: 林语堂的自题联“两脚踏中西文化，一心评宇宙文章”，常被用来概括他的一生。
examples.en: Lin Yutang's own couplet, 'one foot in each culture, my heart appraising the writings of the universe', is often used to sum up his life.

examples.zh: 展览入口处写着“两脚踏中西文化，一心评宇宙文章”，介绍这位作家的志向。
examples.en: At the entrance to the exhibition hung the couplet 'two feet tread Chinese and Western culture, one heart appraises the writings of the universe', introducing the writer's ambition.

story.en: Lin Yutang (1895-1976), who wrote in both Chinese and English and introduced Chinese culture to Western readers, is known for this self-written couplet.
story.zh: 林语堂（1895—1976）中英文兼擅，向西方介绍中国文化，这副对联是他的自题联。

usage.en: Quoted when describing Lin Yutang, or anyone at home in both Chinese and Western culture. It is traditionally attributed to him as a couplet he wrote for himself; the exact date is not certain.
usage.zh: 介绍林语堂，或形容精通中西文化的人时引用。一般认为是他自撰的对联，具体年代不详。

text: 假如我是一只鸟，我也应该用嘶哑的喉咙歌唱
pinyin: jiǎ rú wǒ shì yī zhī niǎo, wǒ yě yīng gāi yòng sī yǎ de hóu lóng gē chàng
literal: if · I · am · one · (measure) · bird, I · also · should · use · hoarse · 's · throat · sing
natural: if I were a bird, I too would sing with a hoarse throat

meaning.en: Ai Qing's opening line: even if it costs him his voice, the poet would sing for the land he loves.
meaning.zh: 艾青的开篇之句：纵使嗓音嘶哑，诗人也要为深爱的土地歌唱。

equivalents: sing though the voice is hoarse
devotion to one's homeland

examples.zh: 朗诵会上，他深情地读起了“假如我是一只鸟，我也应该用嘶哑的喉咙歌唱”。
examples.en: At the poetry reading he recited with feeling, 'if I were a bird, I too would sing with a hoarse throat'.

examples.zh: 她在演讲稿里引用了“假如我是一只鸟，我也应该用嘶哑的喉咙歌唱”，表达对家乡的感情。
examples.en: In her speech she quoted 'if I were a bird, I too would sing with a hoarse throat' to express her feeling for her hometown.

story.en: Ai Qing wrote 'I Love This Land' in November 1938, during the war against Japan, shortly after leaving Wuhan.
story.zh: 1938年11月，抗日战争期间，艾青离开武汉后不久写下《我爱这土地》。

usage.en: Quoted to express devotion to one's country or home town. The poem ends with the famous lines 为什么我的眼里常含泪水？因为我对这土地爱得深沉.
usage.zh: 用来表达对祖国、家乡的深情。全诗结尾是名句“为什么我的眼里常含泪水？因为我对这土地爱得深沉”。

text: 独立寒秋，湘江北去，橘子洲头
pinyin: dú lì hán qiū, xiāng jiāng běi qù, jú zi zhōu tóu
literal: stand · alone · cold · autumn, Xiang · River · north · flow, Orange · Isle · head
natural: alone in the cold autumn, the Xiang River flows north past the tip of Orange Isle

meaning.en: The opening of Mao Zedong's 'Changsha', setting the scene on the Xiang River in late autumn.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《沁园春·长沙》的开头，勾勒出深秋湘江边的景象。

equivalents: standing alone in the cold autumn
the Xiang River flows north

examples.zh: 游客站在橘子洲头，不禁想起“独立寒秋，湘江北去，橘子洲头”。
examples.en: Standing at the tip of Orange Isle, visitors cannot help recalling 'alone in the cold autumn, the Xiang River flows north past Orange Isle'.

examples.zh: 长沙旅游宣传片以“独立寒秋，湘江北去，橘子洲头”作为开场。
examples.en: The Changsha tourist film opens with 'alone in the cold autumn, the Xiang River flows north past Orange Isle'.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'Changsha' (to the tune 沁园春) in the autumn of 1925, as he left Changsha for Guangzhou.
story.zh: 1925年秋，毛泽东离开长沙前往广州时写下《沁园春·长沙》。

usage.en: Quoted in connection with Changsha, the Xiang River and Orange Isle (橘子洲), where the poem is set. Often seen at the site itself.
usage.zh: 多在提到长沙、湘江和橘子洲时引用，橘子洲上也常见此句。

text: 看万山红遍，层林尽染；漫江碧透，百舸争流
pinyin: kàn wàn shān hóng biàn, céng lín jìn rǎn, màn jiāng bì tòu, bǎi gě zhēng liú
literal: look · ten-thousand · hills · red · everywhere, layered · woods · all · dyed; whole · river · green · clear, hundred · boats · compete · to flow
natural: see ten thousand hills red all over, layer on layer of woods dyed; the whole river clear and green, a hundred boats racing

meaning.en: A picture of an autumn landscape in Mao Zedong's 'Changsha': red hills, tinted woods, a clear river and boats vying for the current.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《沁园春·长沙》中的秋景：万山红叶，层林尽染，江水碧透，千帆竞发。

equivalents: a blaze of autumn colour
hills aflame and boats racing on the river

examples.zh: 秋天的香山红叶满山，正是“看万山红遍，层林尽染；漫江碧透，百舸争流”。
examples.en: The Fragrant Hills in autumn, covered in red leaves, are just as the poem says: 'see ten thousand hills red all over, layer on layer of woods dyed; the whole river clear and green, a hundred boats racing'.

examples.zh: 摄影展的主题是“看万山红遍，层林尽染；漫江碧透，百舸争流”。
examples.en: The theme of the photography exhibition was 'see ten thousand hills red all over, layer on layer of woods dyed'.

story.en: From the first half of 'Changsha', in which Mao looks out over the Xiang River in autumn before turning to the question of who will shape the country's future.
story.zh: 出自《沁园春·长沙》上阕，作者先写湘江秋景，再引出“谁主沉浮”的发问。

usage.en: Often quoted for autumn scenery. Parts of it are also used on their own as set phrases (see 万山红遍, 层林尽染, 百舸争流).
usage.zh: 常用来描写秋景，其中“万山红遍”“层林尽染”“百舸争流”也常单独作为成语式短语使用。

text: 北国风光，千里冰封，万里雪飘
pinyin: běi guó fēng guāng, qiān lǐ bīng fēng, wàn lǐ xuě piāo
literal: northern · land · scenery, thousand · li · ice · sealed, ten-thousand · li · snow · flutters
natural: the scenery of the north: a thousand miles sealed in ice, ten thousand miles of drifting snow

meaning.en: The opening of Mao Zedong's 'Snow', picturing the vast frozen north.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《沁园春·雪》的开头，描绘北方冰雪千里的壮阔景象。

equivalents: a thousand miles of ice and snow
a boundless winter landscape

examples.zh: 哈尔滨冰雪节的开幕词引用了“北国风光，千里冰封，万里雪飘”。
examples.en: The opening speech of the Harbin Ice and Snow Festival quoted 'the scenery of the north: a thousand miles sealed in ice, ten thousand miles of drifting snow'.

examples.zh: 飞机掠过东北上空，他望着窗外，想起了“北国风光，千里冰封，万里雪飘”。
examples.en: As the plane passed over the north-east he looked out of the window and thought of 'a thousand miles sealed in ice, ten thousand miles of drifting snow'.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'Snow' in February 1936 in northern Shaanxi, at the end of the Long March.
story.zh: 1936年2月，毛泽东在陕北写下《沁园春·雪》。

usage.en: Quoted for winter scenery in northern China. 千里 and 万里 are poetic exaggeration, not measured distances.
usage.zh: 形容中国北方冬景时引用。“千里”“万里”是诗意的夸张，并非实指距离。

text: 惜秦皇汉武，略输文采；唐宗宋祖，稍逊风骚
pinyin: xī qín huáng hàn wǔ, lüè shū wén cǎi, táng zōng sòng zǔ, shāo xùn fēng sāo
literal: pity · Qin Emperor · Han Wu, slightly · lose · literary talent; Tang Taizong · Song Taizu, a little · yield · poetic gifts
natural: a pity that the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han were a little short on literary grace, and Taizong of Tang and Taizu of Song somewhat lacking in poetry

meaning.en: Mao Zedong's remark in 'Snow' that the great founding emperors of past dynasties were all somewhat lacking in literary talent.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《沁园春·雪》中的评论：历代开国君王都略欠文采诗才。

equivalents: great rulers, but poor poets
mighty in power, modest in letters

examples.zh: 讲到这首词，老师解释了“惜秦皇汉武，略输文采；唐宗宋祖，稍逊风骚”的含义。
examples.en: Discussing this poem, the teacher explained what 'a pity that the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han were a little short on literary grace...' means.

examples.zh: 他半开玩笑地说：“惜秦皇汉武，略输文采；唐宗宋祖，稍逊风骚。”
examples.en: Half joking he said, 'a pity that Qin Shi Huang and Han Wudi were a little short on literary grace, and Tang Taizong and Song Taizu somewhat lacking in poetry'.

story.en: In the second half of 'Snow', Mao surveys famous rulers of Chinese history, each admirable in one respect but lacking in another.
story.zh: 《沁园春·雪》下阕历数中国历史上的著名君主，认为各有所长，也各有所短。

usage.en: Often quoted when comparing power with literary talent. 风骚 refers to the 《诗经》 (Airs of the States) and the 《离骚》, so it means literary excellence in general.
usage.zh: 常在比较权势与文才时引用。“风骚”原指《诗经》国风和《离骚》，泛指文学才华。

text: 一代天骄，成吉思汗，只识弯弓射大雕
pinyin: yī dài tiān jiāo, chéng jí sī hán, zhǐ shí wān gōng shè dà diāo
literal: one · generation · Heaven's · favoured son, Genghis · Khan, only · knew · bend · bow · shoot · big · eagle
natural: the favoured son of his age, Genghis Khan, knew only how to draw his bow and shoot the great eagle

meaning.en: Mao Zedong's line on Genghis Khan: a towering conqueror of his age whose gifts, in the poem's view, ran to warfare rather than letters.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东对成吉思汗的评语：一代英雄，却只擅长弯弓射雕，不长于文采。

equivalents: a mighty warrior, but no poet
a great conqueror, but not a man of letters

examples.zh: 他用“一代天骄，成吉思汗，只识弯弓射大雕”介绍内蒙古大草原的历史。
examples.en: He introduced the history of the Inner Mongolian grasslands with 'the favoured son of his age, Genghis Khan, knew only how to draw his bow and shoot the great eagle'.

examples.zh: 朋友笑着说，他只会打球，真是“一代天骄，成吉思汗，只识弯弓射大雕”。
examples.en: His friend joked that all he could do was play ball, truly 'the favoured son of his age, Genghis Khan, knew only how to draw his bow and shoot the great eagle'.

story.en: In 'Snow' Mao names Genghis Khan among the great rulers of history; the poem is dated February 1936.
story.zh: 毛泽东在《沁园春·雪》（1936年2月）中列举历史上的著名君主，成吉思汗即其中之一。

usage.en: Quoted about Genghis Khan and the Mongol steppe, and sometimes playfully of someone talented in one area only. 天骄 means 'Heaven's favoured son' and was once a title for steppe rulers.
usage.zh: 谈及成吉思汗和蒙古草原时引用，有时也戏指某人只擅长一方面。“天骄”意为“天之骄子”，古时曾用来称草原上的君主。

text: 金沙水拍云崖暖，大渡桥横铁索寒
pinyin: jīn shā shuǐ pāi yún yá nuǎn, dà dù qiáo héng tiě suǒ hán
literal: Golden Sands · water · lap · cloudy · cliffs · warm, Dadu · bridge · span · iron · chains · cold
natural: the Jinsha's waters lap the cloud-high cliffs, warm; the Dadu Bridge spans on its cold iron chains

meaning.en: A couplet from Mao Zedong's 'The Long March' that contrasts the warm cliffs of the Jinsha River with the cold iron chains of the Dadu Bridge.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《七律·长征》中的对句：金沙江畔的云崖温暖，大渡河上的铁索桥寒意逼人。

equivalents: warm cliffs and cold iron chains
the Long March's crossings

examples.zh: 参观泸定桥时，导游念起了“金沙水拍云崖暖，大渡桥横铁索寒”。
examples.en: While visiting the Luding Bridge the guide recited 'the Jinsha's waters lap the cloud-high cliffs, warm; the Dadu Bridge spans on its cold iron chains'.

examples.zh: 纪念馆的展板上写着“金沙水拍云崖暖，大渡桥横铁索寒”。
examples.en: On a display board at the memorial hall was written 'the Jinsha's waters lap the cloud-high cliffs, warm; the Dadu Bridge spans on its cold iron chains'.

story.en: The poem, written in October 1935, recalls the Red Army's crossings of the Jinsha River and the Dadu River during the Long March (1934-36).
story.zh: 1935年10月所作，回顾长征（1934—1936年）中红军渡金沙江、夺大渡河桥的经历。

usage.en: Quoted when speaking about the Long March, the Jinsha River and the Luding (Dadu River) Bridge. The poem was written in October 1935.
usage.zh: 谈及长征、金沙江和泸定桥时引用。此诗作于1935年10月。

text: 更喜岷山千里雪，三军过后尽开颜
pinyin: gèng xǐ mín shān qiān lǐ xuě, sān jūn guò hòu jìn kāi yán
literal: even · delight · Min Mountains · thousand · li · snow, three · armies · pass · after · all · faces brighten
natural: even more joyful, the Min Mountains' thousand miles of snow; once the army has crossed, every face lights up

meaning.en: The closing couplet of Mao Zedong's 'The Long March': after the hardships of the march, crossing the snowy Min Mountains brings smiles.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《七律·长征》的结句：长征路上历尽艰险，翻过千里积雪的岷山后，将士们都露出了笑容。

equivalents: hardship ends in smiles
over the last mountain, faces brighten

examples.zh: 经过几个月的攻关，项目终于完成，大家真是“更喜岷山千里雪，三军过后尽开颜”。
examples.en: After months of hard work the project was finished at last, and everyone was truly 'even more joyful, the Min Mountains' thousand miles of snow; once the army has crossed, every face lights up'.

examples.zh: 老师以“更喜岷山千里雪，三军过后尽开颜”收束了这堂课。
examples.en: The teacher closed the lesson with 'even more joyful, the Min Mountains' thousand miles of snow; once the army has crossed, every face lights up'.

story.en: The last couplet of 'The Long March', written in October 1935 after the Red Army crossed the Min Mountains.
story.zh: 1935年10月，红军翻越岷山后写下的《七律·长征》，这是其结尾对句。

usage.en: Quoted for the relief and joy at the end of a long, hard effort. The Min Mountains are on the border of Sichuan and Gansu.
usage.zh: 用来形容经过漫长艰苦努力后的欣慰与喜悦。岷山位于四川、甘肃交界处。

text: 今日长缨在手，何时缚住苍龙
pinyin: jīn rì cháng yīng zài shǒu, hé shí fù zhù cāng lóng
literal: today · long · tassel-rope · in · hand, when · bind · fast · blue · dragon
natural: today the long rope is in our hands; when shall we bind the azure dragon?

meaning.en: The closing lines of Mao Zedong's 'Mount Liupan': now that the means are in hand, when will the great foe be bound?
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《清平乐·六盘山》的结句：如今大权在握、力量在手，何时能缚住强敌。

equivalents: the means are in hand, when will we succeed?
now we hold the rope, when do we bind the dragon?

examples.zh: 项目负责人在动员会上念道：“今日长缨在手，何时缚住苍龙？”
examples.en: At the mobilisation meeting the project leader declared, 'today the long rope is in our hands; when shall we bind the dragon?'

examples.zh: 纪念馆里展出了这首词，末句“今日长缨在手，何时缚住苍龙”格外醒目。
examples.en: The poem was on display at the memorial hall, and its last line, 'today the long rope is in our hands; when shall we bind the dragon?', stood out.

origin.source: 毛泽东《清平乐·六盘山》（1935年）

story.en: 'Mount Liupan', to the tune 清平乐, was written in October 1935 as the Red Army crossed Liupan Mountain on the last stretch of the Long March.
story.zh: 1935年10月，红军长征最后一段翻越六盘山时，毛泽东写下《清平乐·六盘山》。

usage.en: Quoted as a call to act on a long-held goal. 长缨 is a long tasselled rope or cord; 苍龙 is a dragon, here the enemy. The line echoes the Han story of Zhong Jun, who asked for a long rope to bind the king of Southern Yue.
usage.zh: 用来激励人们完成夙愿。“长缨”指长绳，“苍龙”比喻强敌。此句化用汉代终军请缨缚南越王的典故。
